when: Saturday 10 October 2026 · while you were away
headline: Two records tied, none beaten yet
lede: While you were away, the engine ran 27 rounds of evolution across two runs and wrote 324 programs with Haiku. It rediscovered all 8 known answers and matched the best known graph on two open cases: 160 for degree 4 within 5 steps, and 394 for degree 16 within 3 steps. Both were checked by two independent checkers and rebuilt from scratch. No case has been beaten yet; the closest is degree 7 within 4 steps at 339 of 346.
ideas: Lifts over non-cyclic groups. After I added a helper for 'semidirect product' groups and a hint, Haiku picked it up within one round, and that is how it tied the 160 record.
Arc-extended projective planes: start from the classic plane graph and graft on extra points. This tied the 394 record for degree 16.
Generalized quadrangles for the 4-step cases. It found W(3) from the hint on its very first try.
Crossover programs that bundle the best trick for each case did most of the climbing after round 10.
Zero broken programs in 324 tries. Every Haiku reply compiled and returned a valid graph.
next: Let run 2 finish its 40 rounds (about 3 more hours). It keeps going on its own.
The published construction for the diameter-3 cases is now a helper Haiku can see (it builds 190, 274 and 374 exactly). Next rounds can start from the record instead of 6 below it.
Settle cloud with you watching: open one cloud session in the app and paste the 4-step test. Takes 5 minutes.
If the ties hold and nothing beats them in 40 rounds, switch targets to diameter 5 and 6 with bigger degrees, where the gaps are widest.
cloud: Not solved. A real cloud session started fine, but it went idle and never pushed its results, and I could not read it back from the terminal without an interactive prompt. My own remote-agent option quietly ran on your Mac instead. So everything tonight ran on your Mac. The open question is still whether claude -p works on your subscription inside a cloud machine.
costnote: Haiku calls are cheap: about 0.5 to 1 cent each at API prices. The whole night used about 9% of the weekly allowance on the account, including my own coordinating. The five-hour window never went above 20%.
